session_note: Idaho's 2026 Second Regular Session (68th Legislature) convened 2026-01-12 and is a short annual session; bills not enacted before sine die die and do not carry into a future annual session (unlike Kansas's biennium). legislature.idaho.gov bill-status pages do not print an explicit 'Died' label or a sine die date for bills that stall in committee or in concurrence -- they simply stop recording new actions. For bills in this packet with no action recorded after early-to-mid 2026 (well past any plausible 2026 adjournment, confirmed live on 2026-07-31), that stagnation on the state's own authoritative page is treated as the evidence of failed_died, consistent with how the prior researcher already characterized several of these bills.

new_bills.status: Passed House 65-3-2 (2026-03-20); passed Senate 34-1-0 (2026-03-30); signed by Governor 2026-04-10; Session Law Chapter 335; effective 2026-07-01 via emergency clause.
new_bills.key_provisions: Adds Idaho Code 61-335, titled 'New Large Load and Ratepayer Protection.' Defines a 'new large load' as a service-entrance load increase of 50 MW or more within a rolling 60-month period under a contract entered on or after 2026-07-01 (squarely covers data centers). Requires a PUC-approved service contract before a utility may serve such a load, including a commission 'no harm test'; makes the new large load responsible for its full cost of service (generation, transmission, substation, distribution); bars load-splitting to evade the threshold; requires financial security against stranded costs; and directs the commission to review rates in each general rate case to keep other ratepayers' bills from rising because of the new load.
